text:
Auston Matthews came back from last season's knee surgery looking like the old Matthews, and it hasn't been enough. He has 29 points in 22 games, 12 goals, and the Leafs have lost six straight, a winless homestand that put them last in the Atlantic. Daily Faceoff's Matt Larkin has written that his future in Toronto isn't as settled as it looked in September, with Matthews eligible to sign an extension next July, and the headlines have also picked over his comments backing coach Jim Hiller.

His own game is real. His 10.9 expected goals (the quality of his chances) sit close to his 12 goals, and Toronto has outshot and outchanced opponents with him at five on five. The padding is elsewhere: the Leafs have scored 9.5 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of on-ice luck fades, which is why our range for his scoring rate sits below where he is now. Over his last ten he has 11 points, right on our expected 10.9. The goals have slowed as the team has; we'd watch whether the chances keep coming anyway.
